title: The finite-stage boundary input is a consequence
statement:
The boundary duality input of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]
holds for every separated finite-type $Y/k$ and every finite stage
$A=A_{E,n}$. In particular the canonical evaluation-defined map

$$
\beta_L:i^*D_TL\longrightarrow D_ZRi^!L
$$

is an isomorphism for every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$
between the locally closed pieces in that definition.

proof.text: Work first on the small etale sites with $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $Y$ is Noetherian. Write a locally closed piece $W$ as a closed subscheme of an open $V\subseteq Y$. The Noetherian-open lemma makes $V$ Noetherian and its inclusion quasi-compact, hence finite type by the quasi-compact-open lemma; the closed inclusion is proper and finite type by the closed-immersion lemma. Composing finite generating sets on affine charts proves $W/k$ finite type. Its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $Y/k$, hence is closed; thus $W/k$ is separated. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma applies again to $W$.

source.place: First paragraph: geometry of the pieces

proof.text: On every piece, [thm-fix-general-biduality] gives preservation of $D^b_{ctf}$ by $D_W$ and invertibility of $\delta$. Apply [lem-weil-boundary-dualizing-composition] to the structure maps and to $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$: the etale adjoints restrict to $D^+$, and the counit-compatible composition gives $Ri^!\omega_T\cong\omega_Z$. This also supplies their comparison-class pro-etale transport. No unbounded pro-etale adjunction is required.

source.place: First paragraph: preservation and dualizing-object composition

proof.text:
Fix $L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and put $P=i^*D_TL$ and $U=Ri^!L$. The etale $i^*$ is the exact constant-coefficient inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; [prop-constructible-pullback] therefore makes $P$ bounded constructible. For its Tor bound, use [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] to send $D_TL$ to the finite-Tor pro-etale category, apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] there, and identify its result with $\nu_Z^*P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The converse clause of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] reflects that bound to the bounded etale complex $P$. Thus $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ with no silent identification of the two sites. Apply [lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality] to $D_TL$. It gives an isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha_{D_TL}:Ri^!D_TD_TL\to D_ZP$. Thus
$$\widetilde c_L=\widetilde\alpha_{D_TL}\circ Ri^!\delta_L:U\xrightarrow{\sim}D_ZP.$$
Consequently $U$ is finite-Tor constructible, because $D_ZP$ is so by [thm-fix-general-biduality]. The same argument applied to any $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ shows $Ri^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, in particular for $K=D_TL$. This conclusion used costalk duality and biduality, without using the boundary exchange. Here the tildes distinguish a preservation witness from the evaluation-normalized comparison to be constructed in step 6; no normalization of the costalk lemma is inferred from its statement.

source.place: First paragraph: alpha composed with the double-dual map and the finite-Tor domain

proof.text:
Record the tensor--internal-Hom adjunction used in the remaining map calculations on the actual ringed sites. Given $B,C,H\in D(A_W)$, choose a K-flat flat-term representative $Q$ of $C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $H$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] show that $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,I)$ is a K-injective representative of $R\mathcal Hom(C,H)$. The natural complex isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] identifies the representatives of $R\mathcal Hom(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,H))$ and $R\mathcal Hom(B\otimes^LC,H)$. Taking $H^0$ of derived global sections and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes^LC,H).$$
The counit is evaluation; transposition is natural in all three variables. This proves the needed adjunction from statements about small ringed sites, rather than citing an adjunction for $\mathcal O_X$-modules as though it were an adjunction for etale $A$-modules. Tensor symmetry is the signed interchange of homogeneous factors, $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg x\deg y}y\otimes x$; the two interchanges compose to the identity and respect the total differential.

Write $\mu_N:Ri_!Ri^!N\to N$ for the exceptional counit. For $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ define $q_{M,N}:i^*M\otimes_A^LRi^!N\to Ri^!(M\otimes_A^LN)$ as the transpose of
$$Ri_!(i^*M\otimes_A^LRi^!N)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}M\otimes_A^LRi_!Ri^!N\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu_N}M\otimes_A^LN.$$
The projection formula applies since $M$ is finite-Tor and $Ri^!N$ is bounded constructible by step 3; tensor symmetry gives this order. The exceptional adjunction is the etale ambient one. Transposing the natural projection/counit composite makes $q$ natural in both variables.

source.place: Second paragraph: exceptional tensor comparison q

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-boundary-alpha-normalization] using the tensor-Hom adjunction of step 4 and the preservation established in steps 2--3. Its explicit Hom chain proves that the transpose of
$$r_K=Ri^!(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}\circ\sigma_{Ri^!D_TK,i^*K}$$
is the isomorphism $\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K$. This fixes the evaluation normalization, rather than inferring it from the existence-only costalk statement. Put $c_L=\alpha_{D_TL}\circ Ri^!\delta_L:U\xrightarrow{\sim}D_ZP$. Both factors are isomorphisms. The preliminary $\widetilde c_L$ of step 3 served only to establish the finite-Tor domain.

source.place: Second paragraph: normalized alpha and c

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-duality-pairing], $\delta_L$ is the transpose of evaluation after tensor symmetry. The defining transpose equation is therefore
$$\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ(\delta_L\otimes1_{D_TL})=\mathrm{ev}_L\circ\sigma_{L,D_TL}.$$
This is an equality of maps $L\otimes^LD_TL\to\omega_T$, with the same signed symmetry as in step 4. No invertibility is needed for this identity.

source.place: Second paragraph: the evaluation identity used to identify the canonical boundary map

proof.text:
Let
$$b_L=Ri^!\mathrm{ev}_L\circ q_{D_TL,L}:P\otimes^LU\longrightarrow\omega_Z.$$
This is the pairing whose transpose defines $\beta_L$ in [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. Let $t(c_L)=\mathrm{ev}_P\circ(c_L\otimes1_P)$ be the transpose of $c_L$. The formula for $r$ in step 6, naturality of $q$ in its second variable, naturality of tensor symmetry, and step 7 give the following equality of maps $U\otimes^LP\to\omega_Z$:
$$\begin{aligned}
t(c_L)&=r_{D_TL}\circ(Ri^!\delta_L\otimes1_P)\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ\sigma_{D_TL,D_TD_TL}\circ(1_{D_TL}\otimes\delta_L)\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ(\delta_L\otimes1_{D_TL})\circ\sigma_{D_TL,L}\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_L\circ\sigma_{L,D_TL}\circ\sigma_{D_TL,L}\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=b_L\circ\sigma_{U,P}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last line uses $\sigma_{L,D_TL}\sigma_{D_TL,L}=1$. Thus $c_L$ and $\beta_L$ are the two currying maps of this same pairing, in opposite tensor orders.

source.place: Second paragraph: identify the transpose of alpha composed with Ri! delta

proof.text:
Naturality of evaluation for $c_L:U\to D_ZP$ gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_U\circ(D_Zc_L\otimes1_U)=\mathrm{ev}_{D_ZP}\circ(1_{D_ZD_ZP}\otimes c_L).$$
Precomposing with $\delta_P\otimes1_U$ and using the transpose identity from step 7 on $Z$ shows that the transpose of $D_Z(c_L)\circ\delta_P$ is $b_L$. Uniqueness under the adjunction of step 4 therefore gives the specified-map identity
$$\beta_L=D_Z(c_L)\circ\delta_P.$$
Both factors are isomorphisms: $c_L$ is an isomorphism by step 6, a functor sends its inverse to an inverse, and $\delta_P$ is an isomorphism by [thm-fix-general-biduality], since $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Hence the canonical evaluation-defined boundary map is an isomorphism.

source.place: First displayed double-duality composite and second paragraph: its inverse is the canonical beta

proof.text:
For the evaluation compatibility, fix $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. The transpose of $\beta_{D_TK}\circ i^*\delta_K$ is
$$Ri^!\mathrm{ev}_{D_TK}\circ q_{D_TD_TK,D_TK}\circ(i^*\delta_K\otimes1_{Ri^!D_TK}).$$
Naturality of $q$ and step 7 rewrite this as
$$Ri^!(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}:i^*K\otimes^LRi^!D_TK\longrightarrow\omega_Z.$$
On the other hand the transpose of $D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{i^*K}$ is $r_K\circ\sigma_{i^*K,Ri^!D_TK}$, by naturality of evaluation and the defining transpose of $\delta_{i^*K}$. This is the very same displayed map, by the formula for $r_K$ in step 6. Uniqueness of transposition yields
$$\beta_{D_TK}\circ i^*\delta_K=D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{i^*K}.$$
Composing with $(D_Z\alpha_K)^{-1}$ gives exactly the double-dual compatibility required in [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. The two cancellations of symmetry use its involutivity, so they include the Koszul signs.

source.place: Second paragraph: explicit equation for compatibility with the restricted double-dual morphism

proof.text: For the pro-etale realization put $C_W=\nu_W^*$. Every bounded constructible input has an etale-origin representative by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] preserves and reflects its finite Tor interval. The ordinary restriction is identified by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The specified exceptional restriction is $C_Zi^\times R\nu_{T,*}$; the site-comparison unit identifies its value on $C_TN$ with $C_Zi^\times N$. These are bounded-below inputs, so the comparison-class adjunction applies. For $i$, choose its identity-open compactification. Its finite-type source has a finite dimension bound by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, checking the class-adjunction dimension hypothesis.

source.place: Second paragraph realized on pro-etale site: origin and exceptional restriction

proof.text:
Use the identity-open compactification of $i$, so $F_e=Ri_{e,*}$ and $F_p=Ri_{p,*}$. Let $\eta_B:F_pC_ZB\xrightarrow{\sim}C_TF_eB$ be the inverse of the named canonical direct-image mate. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-boundary-proetale-projection-comparison] use exactly this mate and the monoidal tensor-pullback comparison. It gives
$$\mu^p_{C_TN}=C_T(\mu^e_N)\eta_{i^\times N},\qquad \eta_{B\otimes i_e^*M}\pi_p=C_T(\pi_e)(\eta_B\otimes1).$$
Thus both exceptional counits and the named projection transformations, including their inverses on the finite-Tor inputs of step 3, agree under comparison.

source.place: Second paragraph realized on pro-etale site: counit and projection normalization

proof.text: Check the hypotheses of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison]. The constant sheaf $A_W$ is locally constant finite, hence constructible, and $A_W\otimes_A^LN=N$ shows Tor interval $[0,0]$. On a K-injective representative $I$ of $H$, the internal Hom complex from $A_W$ is $I$ itself, so $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_W,H)\cong H$. Therefore $\omega_{W,e}=D_WA_W$ is bounded finite-Tor constructible by biduality. Every first variable needed below is finite-Tor: the inputs and their duals by step 2, ordinary and exceptional restrictions by step 3, and further duals by step 2. The comparison lemma consequently applies with second variable $\omega_{W,e}$. Denote its dualizing comparison by $w_W$ and its internal-Hom comparison by $\chi_{W,H}:C_WD_WH\cong D_W^pC_WH$. It identifies evaluation and its double-dual transpose.

source.place: Second paragraph realized on pro-etale site: finite-duality comparison hypotheses

proof.text:
The counit and projection identities of step 12 satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-boundary-proetale-q-compatibility]. It identifies $q^p_{C_TM,C_TN}$ with $C_Zq^e_{M,N}$ and the transposes of all the evaluation/symmetry pairings used here. In conjunction with $w,\chi$ from step 13, the explicit formula for $r$ in step 6 identifies $\alpha^p$ with the comparison of $\alpha^e$. The formula for $b$ in step 8 identifies the canonical $\beta^p$ with the comparison of $\beta^e$. Applying the comparison to the two sides of the equalities of steps 9--10, and using its identified double-dual transposes, proves invertibility of $\beta^p$ and
$$\beta^p_{D_T^pC_TK}\circ i_p^*\delta^p_{C_TK}=D_Z^p(\alpha^p_{C_TK})\circ\delta^p_{i_p^*C_TK}.$$
Together with preservation from step 2, these are precisely the two clauses of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input].

source.place: Second paragraph realized on pro-etale site: transport of the canonical maps and compatibility

split_report.summary: Repair of the human long-step return: keep the statement and Lean record unchanged, and retain all unflagged proof steps (with renumbered references). Former step 1 now cites the bounded-below dualizing-composition lemma, former step 4 cites evaluation-normalized alpha, and former step 9 cites the proper projection/counit comparison and exceptional-q/pairing comparison. The remaining geometry, tensor-Hom calculation, coefficient hypothesis checks and beta/delta equations stay in the item. Four new nodes are statement-only; all fourteen proof steps have fewer than 2000 characters.
split_report.blueprint: First paragraph: steps 1--3 establish preservation and the costalk domain. Second paragraph: steps 4--10 give the tensor-Hom adjunction, normalized alpha, canonical beta and delta compatibility. Steps 11--14 give the same named maps on the pro-etale realization.

tool_uses.why: Closed immersions are proper, providing the identity-open-part compactification used for the etale adjunction.
Exactness of constant-coefficient etale module pullback makes the etale restriction bounded before reflecting the Tor interval.
Etale constructibility of the ordinary closed restriction, so the pro-etale pullback lemma is not silently read as an etale statement.
Ambient etale adjunction for a closed immersion (compactification with identity open part); not an ambient pro-etale adjunction.
Generic ringed-site resolution tool used to derive the actual tensor-Hom bijection, without assuming an O_X-specific theorem applies.
Generic small ringed-site K-injective existence used in the tensor-Hom deduction.
Generic K-flat/K-injective Hom-complex lemma (Stacks 0A96).
Generic ringed-site isomorphism of Hom complexes (Stacks 0A90), not its scheme-specialized consequences.
Generic ringed-site H^0(RHom)=Hom lemma (Stacks 08JA).
Finite-stage projection map, used only for a closed immersion and constructible finite-Tor tensor factor, to normalize q and alpha.
Generic site-comparison equivalence supplies etale-origin representatives for all the pro-etale inputs.
Generic ordinary restriction comparison fixes the same pullback in the two realizations.
Generic full faithfulness/unit comparison reduces the transported exceptional functor on etale-origin inputs.
Generic monoidal derived pullback comparison for the comparison morphism of ringed sites.
The counit-compatible restricted adjunction transports the etale map calculation without requiring a nonexistent global pro-etale ambient adjoint.
Finite-type schemes over the field are Noetherian, needed for the etale adjunctions; the unit supplies no geometric permanence lemma.
The open containing a locally closed piece is Noetherian and quasi-compact; generic geometric permanence.
The open factor of a locally closed piece is finite type; generic geometric permanence.
Over Spec k bounds the dimension of the chosen finite-type compactification, checking the comparison-class adjunction hypothesis.
Supplies the precise ordinary counit normalization needed to compare the named projection maps, beyond an existence-only direct-image comparison.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q67-2fd9cc6f0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole delivery against the master and main-20261015 blueprint proofs; they agree. The item's statement is unchanged. Each of the 14 steps is under 2000 characters, and I checked every one against the statements it cites. Step 3: P = i^*D_TL is constructible by exactness and prop-constructible-pullback. Its Tor bound comes from comparison clauses (i) and (ii) of lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude. The costalk lemma is used for existence only, with the ambient closed adjoint from thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint. Step 4 rests on Stacks 06YS, 0A96, 0A90 and 08JA. I recomputed the equations of steps 7-10: the transposes, the naturality of q, the symmetries and the dinaturality of evaluation. They give β_L = D_Z(c_L)δ_P and exactly the δ-compatibility the definition requires. Step 11 checks dim Z ≤ d for thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class through 0A3V. Step 12 uses the inverse of the named canonical mate b_u. Step 13 checks the hypotheses of the finite-duality site comparison. The four new statements are true. In the alpha lemma, Yoneda in D^b_ctf(Z) applied to id_{GD_TK} gives the F-adjoint ev(μ⊗1)PF^{-1}, which equals the adjoint of r_K. In the dualizing lemma, the right adjoints preserve D^+ because compact support has finite amplitude, and the mate of the D^+ composition then gives i^×ω_T ≅ ω_Z and its unit transport. The projection and q comparisons are formal transports through the class adjunction, the counit-normalized b_u and the monoidal comparison 07A4. Edge cases Z = ∅, i = id and K = 0 hold. None of the four duplicates an existing node: I compared them with lem-sf-mate, fix-prop-adjunctions(3), pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition, lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact, lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate and lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison. None restates a clause of the item, and there is no cycle. Every statement the steps cite is in the unit route or among the 20 declared tool uses, all of which I accept. No SGA source is used. FIX (B3): I added two missing definition citations to two new nodes. lem-weil-boundary-alpha-normalization now cites def-amb-etale-compact-support and def-kun-projection-formula-map. lem-weil-boundary-proetale-q-compatibility now cites def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed and def-kun-projection-formula-map.
